screening_decisions.reason: Explicitly described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial evaluating systemic inosiplex in patients with alopecia totalis. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized, placebo-controlled trial evaluating systemic oral prednisolone pulse therapy in patients with extensive alopecia areata. Meets all selection criteria.
Prospective, randomized, controlled, investigator-blinded trial evaluating topical betamethasone formulations for mild-to-moderate alopecia areata. Meets all selection criteria.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled study (RCT) evaluating topical minoxidil in extensive alopecia areata, alopecia totalis, and alopecia universalis. Meets all selection criteria.
Double-blind trial with randomized assignment to minoxidil or placebo evaluating topical minoxidil for extensive alopecia areata. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized double-blind design evaluating topical diphenylcyclopropenone with or without topical minoxidil for chronic severe alopecia areata. Meets all selection criteria.

Patients were randomly assigned to receive topical cyclosporine, PUVA, or intravenous thymopentin. This is an RCT evaluating topical and systemic interventions for alopecia totalis/universalis. Meets all selection criteria.

Uncontrolled pilot study in six patients with extensive alopecia areata. No randomization or control group described; different scalp areas received different concentrations in a non-randomized manner. Does not meet the RCT criterion.
Randomized trial comparing topical cyclosporin A in liposomal vehicle versus vehicle alone for alopecia areata. Meets all selection criteria.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled study (RCT) evaluating systemic imipramine in patients with alopecia areata. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized assignment to topical immunotherapy, systemic interferon alpha, or combination for chronic severe alopecia areata. Meets all selection criteria.
Double-blind study comparing topical cyclosporin A to placebo in alopecia areata. Implicitly an RCT. Meets all selection criteria.
Explicitly described as a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating topical clobetasol propionate foam for alopecia areata. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized, controlled trial evaluating systemic prednisone with or without topical minoxidil for alopecia areata, including alopecia totalis/universalis. Meets all selection criteria.

This abstract appears to summarize clinical experience and multiple prior studies (e.g., 'The results of these studies will be discussed') rather than reporting a single primary RCT. It lacks a clear description of randomization and control for the overall 90-patient cohort. Treated as a summary/review or case series.

Described as a controlled trial comparing active therapies versus placebo in patchy alopecia areata. While the abstract does not explicitly state 'randomized', the term 'controlled trial' in this clinical context is interpreted conservatively as likely an RCT. Meets selection criteria.
Cross-sectional survey/questionnaire study evaluating patient illness perceptions. No intervention is evaluated, and it is not an RCT.
Methodological commentary paper discussing when randomised trials are unnecessary. Not a trial evaluating an intervention for alopecia areata.
Explicitly described as a randomized, double-blind, controlled trial evaluating topical essential oil aromatherapy versus carrier oil control for alopecia areata. Meets all selection criteria.
Narrative review/update article summarizing pathogenesis and treatments. Not a primary RCT.
Retrospective population-based epidemiological descriptive study assessing incidence and natural history. Not an RCT and does not evaluate an intervention.
Observational cohort study examining prognostic factors in patients treated with diphenylcyclopropenone. No control group or randomization described. Not an RCT.

Patients were divided into three groups matched for age and sex, but the abstract does not describe randomization. The use of matching rather than random allocation suggests this may be a non-randomized controlled trial. Does not clearly meet the RCT criterion.
Review article discussing genetic basis of alopecia areata. No intervention evaluated; not an RCT.
Methodology paper discussing quality assessment of controlled trials. Not a primary trial evaluating an intervention for alopecia areata.
